match._comment: Referee. immobilizationCountS is the count; countGraceS how long a robot must look stuck before it starts (absorbs hazard bounces). Robots parked by choice, shoving, or pinned are never counted. pinLimitS before RELEASE!, then pinReleaseS before a control penalty.
match._separate: Two robots locked together (in contact, both trying to drive, neither moving) for separateAfterS seconds are pulled apart by the referee, as on the show. Found by tools/stress.js: two spinners hooked together for 150 s.

judging._comment: Each judge splits each category's points by share; judgeLean is how far one judge's read can drift (seeded). Keep the total points odd so a card cannot tie.

damage.comment: All damage balance lives here, never in code. hpPerKilojoule sets the global scale: a part's hp is in the same currency, so a 640 hp bar hitting an 820 hp AR500 plate is a readable trade. Tune this block first; it is the only place that decides how long a fight lasts.
damage._transfer: Fraction of a weapon's stored energy actually delivered by one hit. A spinner almost never lands a square hit; this is the biggest source of fight-to-fight variance.
damage._severity: Thresholds as a fraction of the struck part's full hp, for choosing effects and commentary.
damage._armor: While a panel still has condition, only this fraction of damage reaches what is behind it. Once the panel is gone, everything does.
damage._pierce: Extra pass-through per unit of weapon concentration above 1.5 - hammers and crushers punch through armour a wide bar only dents.
damage._classScale: Per weapon class multiplier on the hp a hit does - the balance pass's lever, set in physics with tools/balance.sh. Missing means 1.
damage._vulnerability: Per-category multiplier on damage reaching a part. Electronics and batteries hate shock; wheels get torn off; the chassis is the last thing to go.
damage._condition: Condition bands. A part is impaired below `impaired`, barely working below `critical`, dead at zero.
damage._degrade: What a part at ZERO condition still delivers, as a fraction of its rated figure. Linear between there and 1.0. Only the weapon and armour drop to nothing.
damage._electronics: A failing radio/ESC drops out intermittently before it dies. Dropouts per second at zero condition.
damage._ko: A bot is out when its chassis is destroyed, or when it cannot move and is counted out.

weapons._comment: What each weapon class does to what it hits beyond hp (js/sim/combat.js): the throw, the flip, the lift, the grip. The balance pass (Stage 6, tools/balance.sh) tunes these in physics, then the resolver is re-fitted to match.
weapons._kinetic: A rotor's hit throws the victim through the struck point: kineticImpulsePerKJ N*s per kJ delivered, kineticLift the upward share by class (verticals launch), recoil the share the spinner takes back.
weapons._rotorSpend: The least share of its stored energy a rotor loses on any landed hit - a bar that connects stops, and has to spool again. Drums keep the most.
weapons._wedgeDeflect: A rotor striking a wedge, fork or plow glances off it: only transfer[class] of its energy goes in (a horizontal bar rides straight up a wedge; a vertical's tooth bites the lip), and a horizontal is thrown up by liftAttacker of the throw.
weapons._zones: Hammers, flippers, lifters and crushers act on whatever is in the volume they sweep while they fire, not on their parked collider.

pit._comment: Stage 7 - js/logic/pit.js. Damage stays on a robot between fights; the pit window (minutes until its next fight, by stage) times the crew size is the crew-minutes it gets. Repair minutes and cost per hp come from parts.json; labour from economy.json repairs. Tuned with tools/pitcheck.js: a light fight is fixed with time to spare, a heavy one forces choices.
pit._windows: Wall-clock minutes between a robot's fights at each stage.
pit._patch: A patch brings a part back to patchTo of its hp in patchMinutesFactor of the minutes a proper repair of the same hp would take.
pit._totaled: A part below totaledBelow is mangled past repairing: replace it or fight without it. One whose full repair would cost totaledRepairCostRatio of a new one can be repaired, but the pit flags a replacement as the better buy (and the crew's plan takes it).
pit._replaceMinutes: Crew-minutes to swap in a fresh part, by category.
pit._offseason: Between seasons every robot is rebuilt; the player pays this share of the full repair bill (no pit clock, no overtime).

resolver._comment: The fast fight resolver (js/logic/resolver.js), for AI-vs-AI fights in a season. Calibrated against real physics bouts: tools/physdata.js records a dataset, tools/fitresolver.js scores the resolver against it. Tune here, never in code.
resolver._multibot: Multibot units land less (multibotEdge) and are easier to hit, beach and flip (multibotExposure). Physics fights a multibot as its main unit, so these are set to put multibots near an even record, not fitted.

limits._comment: Sanity limits on a robot body, applied every physics step (js/sim/robot_sim.js). Real fights never reach them; they catch solver glitches - a robot squeezed between a hazard and another robot once left the arena at 20 m/s.

difficulty._comment: Settings -> Difficulty, changeable at any time (js/logic/settings.js). skillBonus is added to the AI driver's skill (0..1) in fights against you; adaptOptions is how many pre-fight setups an opponent tests against you (0 = it never adapts) and adaptFights how many trial fights each; learnRate scales how fast every AI learns from its fights (in the fight, between fights, in the pit and the off-season); aiBudget scales the AI teams' off-season money; purse scales what you earn.
